clue.text: Vessel holding medicine for upsets

definitions.note: a plural noun: accidents where things are knocked over

indicators.note: the vessel is said to hold the medicine, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship, a vessel
a pill is a dose of medicine

explanation.surface: A container with medicine in it is kept for stomach upsets.
explanation.definitionFit: Spills are accidents in which something is knocked over, which is what upsets means as a noun.

clue.text: Weather forecast favourable — fear it's incorrect

indicators.note: the letters are set out in an incorrect order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone worries the sunny forecast is wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Set fair is a barometer reading predicting settled, fine weather.

clue.text: Engaged in current affairs?

parts.note: the surface means following the news; read literally it is being in a current of water, like a fish

explanation.surface: Someone is busy with news and politics.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means fully involved in what is going on socially, as a fish moves with the stream.

clue.text: Pulse is fast — over one fifty

indicators.note: in a down answer the first piece sits over the others

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Someone over fifty has a racing pulse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' and 'fast' suggest a heartbeat, but a pulse here is an edible seed and fast means abstain.
explanation.definitionFit: Pulses are edible legume seeds such as peas, beans and the small lens-shaped seed of this plant.

clue.text: Hurry to play set point

indicators.note: the letters are made to play about, so they are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A tennis player rushes to serve at set point.
explanation.definitionFit: To tell someone to get a move on is an idiom urging them to go faster.

clue.text: Journey in the fall

definitions.meaning: a stumble that sends someone over

explanation.surface: A tumble while travelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an excursion and also a stumble.

clue.text: Ibsen hero shows unusual energy in physical exercise

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are put inside the two letters for exercise

parts.note: PT is physical training, school exercise classes

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters are arranged in an uncommon order

explanation.surface: A dramatic character displays remarkable vigour at the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' turns ENERGY into EERGYN, which goes 'in' PT.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibsen's verse drama is named after its wandering Norwegian protagonist.

clue.text: Many a safari included this African lake at one time

definitions.text: this African lake at one time

indicators.note: the run of letters is included within the clue's words

explanation.surface: Many safari trips used to visit a certain lake in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Nyasa was the colonial name of Lake Malawi in East Africa, hence at one time.

clue.text: He will have marked cards, of course

definitions.text: He will have marked cards, of course

parts.words: He will have marked cards, of course
parts.note: the surface suggests a card cheat; the cards are racecards marked with picks, and of course means at a racecourse

explanation.surface: A cheat naturally plays with marked cards.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing adviser marks his choices on the racecards he sells at the track.

clue.text: Carrying a small rum and gin cocktail

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits such as rum

indicators.note: a cocktail is a mixture, so the letters of gin are mixed up

explanation.surface: Someone is carrying a short rum and a gin cocktail at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Toting is an informal synonym for carrying or lugging something around.

clue.text: Got rid of electric current and got gas

parts.note: to fire an employee is to get rid of them
AMP is short for ampere, the unit of electric current

explanation.surface: Someone sacked the electrician and was left with gas instead of power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and got' is a link: the first 'got' belongs to the first piece, the second leads to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Firedamp is the miners' name for the explosive methane found in coal mines.

clue.text: Separate partnership?

parts.note: read as an instruction to split a couple, or as a phrase for a marriage that ends

explanation.surface: A question about splitting up a business partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: The legal ending of a marriage separates the partners.

clue.text: Robust anger with which father sent back the drink

indicators.note: the whole run of pieces is sent back, so it is read from right to left

parts.note: a robust person is fit and healthy
ire is a literary word for anger
pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: An angry father furiously returns a drink he did not order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent back' covers all three pieces at once, so the father comes first in the answer although the clue names him last.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperitif is an alcoholic drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite.

clue.text: Horrified -has the wrong tag showing outside

indicators.note: the jumbled word is shown on the outside, wrapped around the other piece
set wrong means the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone is appalled that a wrong price tag is visible on a garment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' looks like a verb but is part of the letters; 'wrong' jumbles the tag and 'showing outside' wraps it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Aghast means struck with shock or dismay, much the same as appalled.

clue.text: Measure lawyers try to ban

parts.note: an em is a printer's measure of width
the Bar is the collective name for barristers
to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: Lawyers attempt to bring in a prohibition.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official prohibition, especially on trade.

clue.text: Disagreements in the ranks

definitions.meaning: quarrels or arguments, pronounced to rhyme with cows
lines of seats or people side by side, pronounced to rhyme with toes

explanation.surface: There is discord among the soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both quarrels and lines or tiers, the two senses having different pronunciations.

clue.text: English naval officer is about to impress

indicators.note: the officer is placed around the other letter, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: a commander is a senior naval officer

explanation.surface: A naval officer from England is trying to make a good impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impress' is not about making an impression: it is the old sense of forcing men into naval service.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress is to seize for official use, just as to requisition or seize a ship or vehicle.

clue.text: Vanish with girl quietly, so to speak

parts.note: Eva is a girl's name
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, quietly
to orate is to make a speech

explanation.surface: A man disappears with a girl, talking softly, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so' is a link word joining the last piece to the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To evaporate is to disappear, like liquid turning to vapour.

clue.text: Andy's one to provide a non-committal answer

definitions.text: Andy's one to provide a non-committal answer

parts.words: Andy's one to provide a non-committal answer
parts.note: Andy is a man who answers neither way; the name also holds the word joining the two short replies

explanation.surface: A man called Andy is known for evasive answers.
explanation.definitionFit: Answering both ways at once is the classic hedging reply that commits to nothing.

clue.text: Business advertisement on TV

definitions.meaning: an adjective sense: relating to trade
a broadcast advert in a break between programmes

explanation.surface: A business placing an advert on television.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes trade and is also the noun for a television advert.

clue.text: Prevail over island uprising, being efficient

parts.note: to cap something is to outdo or top it

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Elba is the Mediterranean island of Napoleon's exile

explanation.surface: A competent leader puts down a revolt on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Capable means competent and able to do a job well.

clue.text: Second generation savant

parts.note: an age can mean a generation of people

explanation.surface: A child of a second generation turns out to be a scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: A sage is a wise and learned person, which is what a savant is.

clue.text: Speak fast

definitions.meaning: to put into words, verbal sense
an adjective sense: rapid, as of a train or delivery

explanation.surface: Talk quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to put into words and also describes a rapid train or delivery.

clue.text: Gaoled drunken ancient

indicators.note: drunken suggests letters staggering about out of their order

explanation.surface: An old drunk was locked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has existed for ages is ancient.

clue.text: A column I will condense into a short paragraph

indicators.note: one piece is put into the other, which is split around it

parts.note: PAR is a common short form of paragraph
I will condensed is the contraction I'll

explanation.surface: A newspaper columnist promises to boil a column down to a brief paragraph.
explanation.definitionFit: A pillar is an upright supporting post, such as a column in a building.

clue.text: Money is a bait that takes many in

indicators.note: the bait takes another piece in, so the letter goes inside it

parts.note: a lure is a bait used to attract fish or prey
C, the Roman numeral for a hundred, stands for many

explanation.surface: Cash is the bait that draws many people in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' completes the container: the bait takes C in.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucre is money, especially when gained dishonourably, as in filthy lucre.

clue.text: Urge pa, go around with people of the same generation

indicators.note: the letters are sent around into a different order

explanation.surface: A child urges their father to get going and join others his age.
explanation.definitionFit: An age group is a band of people born around the same time.

clue.text: A vessel has got right inside the harbour

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a pot is a vessel for cooking or holding liquid

explanation.surface: A ship has come right into the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A port is a harbour town or a place where ships load and unload.

clue.text: Champion desert scenery

parts.note: to back a cause is to champion it
to drop someone is to desert or abandon them

explanation.surface: A champion abandons the desert landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: A backdrop is a painted cloth hung at the back of a stage as scenery.

clue.text: To practise with wisdom that's the job of a doctor

parts.note: to do something is to practise or perform it
sage as a noun can mean wisdom, as in sagacity

explanation.surface: Practising medicine wisely is what being a doctor is about.
explanation.definitionFit: Deciding how much of a medicine a patient takes is a doctor's task, so the amount prescribed fits.

clue.text: This canine is a biter on sight

indicators.note: in an across answer one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: the eye is the organ of sight
a tooth is something that bites

explanation.surface: A dog that bites as soon as it sees you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'canine' looks like a dog, but it is the pointed tooth of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper canine is called by this name because it sits below the eye.

clue.text: Neat soft-drink dispensers

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, and milk is the soft drink they dispense

explanation.surface: Tidy machines selling fizzy drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: A cow's milk-producing glands are what dispense its milk.
